statement: AC-7 list of user-visible backend messages that say "resource type" today and their new text: (1) "Resource type not found." -> "Resource schema not found." (update schema, delete schema, create instance, list instances); (2) "Only the group owner may create a resource type." -> "Only the group owner may create a resource schema."; (3) "Only the group owner may update a resource type." -> "Only the group owner may update a resource schema."; (4) "Only the group owner may delete a resource type." -> "Only the group owner may delete a resource schema."; (5) "Resource type name cannot be empty." -> "Resource schema name cannot be empty.". Messages that already say "schema" ("A schema with this name already exists in the group.") are unchanged.
The message "Either GroupId or ResourceTypeId must be provided." is added to the AC-7 list although it does not contain the words "resource type": it names the old field.
default_chosen: "Either GroupId or ResourceSchemaId must be provided."
rationale: After the rename the parameter is resourceSchemaId; a message naming a parameter that no longer exists would mislead the caller. One string literal in one handler.
consequence_if_wrong: One 400 message differs from today in one word; revert is a one-line change.

statement: Test code is renamed with the production code: folder ResourceTypes/ -> ResourceSchemas/, test classes and methods, ResourcesResourceTypeFactory -> ResourcesResourceSchemaFactory, ResourcesTestClient methods, ManagementGroupsTestClient.ResourcesAllResourceTypesDeletedAsync and its raw SQL (resources.resource_schemas), comments and assertion messages. Existing tests keep their arrange/assert logic - they are the regression net for AC-1 - only names, routes and field names change.
default_chosen: Rename everything; after the story a case-insensitive search for "resource[ _]?type" in backend/src finds only historical migration files (and their Designer files) and nothing in frontend/src.
rationale: Owner wish in story.md "Notes for discovery": full depth including tests. Leaving old names in tests keeps the old word alive in every later story of the epic.
consequence_if_wrong: No runtime effect; a later mechanical rename of test code.

statement: Frontend code is renamed in full: hand-written DTOs and methods in resources-api.service.ts (ResourceSchemaSummaryDto, ResourceSchemaDetailDto, getResourceSchemas, getResourceSchema, createResourceSchema, updateResourceSchema, deleteResourceSchema, URLs /resources/schemas, payload field resourceSchemaId), their callers (group-context.store, schema-designer-page, create-resource-modal, resources-panel, group-detail-page) and resources-panel.component.spec.ts. The two generated files (api/Resources.ts, api/data-contracts.ts) are regenerated from the new swagger with swagger-typescript-api; if regeneration cannot reproduce the current file layout, the old identifiers are replaced by hand in those two files.

rationale: AC-8 needs the service to call the new addresses; the generated class is imported nowhere (ASM-9), so its exact generation command has no runtime effect, but stale /resources/types paths in it would keep the old word in the frontend.
consequence_if_wrong: Generated client drifts from the swagger or keeps old names; no runtime effect because nothing imports the class; fix is a regeneration.

statement: "The same response as recorded" in AC-10, AC-11 and AC-12 is read together with AC-7 and DEC-2: status codes, error codes resources_forbidden / resources_domain and body shapes are identical to the baseline; message texts that said "resource type" carry the AC-7 wording; the 409 code is the DEC-2 value.

statement: The red-first proof (constitution V) is run for the contract criteria only: AC-1, AC-2, AC-6, AC-7, AC-10, AC-11, AC-12. The tests of AC-9, AC-13 and AC-14 are written in the same blind pass but pass as soon as the developer's migration exists, which the fixed phase order places before the blind tests.
default_chosen: red-first-prover is called with --ac AC-1,AC-2,AC-6,AC-7,AC-10,AC-11,AC-12; AC-9, AC-13 and AC-14 are guarded by migration-check + G2b and by their tests at the gate; the exception is listed in plan.md Complexity Tracking and shown to the owner at G2.
rationale: AC-9, AC-13 and AC-14 are about the migration itself; a test of the migration cannot fail after the migration exists, and the runbook order is skeleton -> developer migration -> blind tests -> behaviour. Moving the migration after the behaviour phase would leave the writer's gate red by construction.
consequence_if_wrong: If the owner wants red-first for the database criteria too, the delivery order for this story must change (blind tests before the migration step) - a conductor-level change, no code impact.
